Maintain normal risk, add on dips to high-momentum AI plays, and avoid chasing DIVA's speculative spike without earnings confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US IRA-driven manufacturing and tax-credit tailwinds continue to structurally favor US solar equipment and EPC names, decoupling them from emerging-market volatility.

Grid-scale storage and AI-driven power demand are re-rating independent power producers (CEG, VST, NRG) as baseload clean firming assets, a durable premium over pure-play solar.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US-listed solar and independent power names (FSLR, RUN, SEDG, ARRY) as US outperformance (+1.03%) versus Indonesia (-1.54%) signals capital rotation into policy-backed US clean energy, while ID exposure remains a laggard—overweight US names, underweight local until clarity on Indonesia's renewable tariff reform emerges.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

Regulatory stability and food-security policies are creating a supportive backdrop for domestic consumer manufacturers, reducing input-cost volatility and boosting margin predictability.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap FMCG names with confirmed volume breakouts (JELI, IATA, BACH) while avoiding large-cap laggards; the sector's mild aggregate gain masks strong rotational momentum into smaller consumer plays. Position for 2-4 week continuation as US-listed peers (+0.46%) confirm demand, but trim into any 15%+ single-day spikes to lock gains.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's e-commerce penetration, still below 20% of retail, drives double-digit parcel volume growth that structurally benefits domestic last-mile operators like MITI and TRUK.

Urbanization and the rise of on-demand delivery in Jakarta/Surabaya create durable demand for taxi-based and micro-freight logistics (TAXI, LOPI), insulated from US trade cycles.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics selectively on domestic names (MITI, TRUK) riding e-commerce parcel volume and port efficiency gains; US weakness is a headwind only for exporters. Accumulate TAXI/LOPI as urban last-mile proxies with tariff-free growth. Trim any US-exposed positions. Sector signal NORMAL supports adding on dips, not chasing +30% spikes.
